TYPE: photo
SUBJECT: A formal meeting around a long light-wood conference table in a government-style room, viewed down its length. On the right side sits a man in a dark suit with white hair (resembling Benjamin Netanyahu) speaking with hands clasped, flanked by suited aides; on the left sit several bearded men in black hats and black coats (ultra-Orthodox officials) listening. The table is set with small black desk microphones, white tented name cards, wooden holders of yellow pencils, paper cups, a glass water pitcher, and notepads; behind them the wall holds two large topographic relief maps and a gray-toned painting.

TYPE: art
SUBJECT: A political cartoon in bold marker style: a panicked Uncle Sam in star-spangled top hat and striped pants sprints left-to-right sweating, while the Statue of Liberty grimaces and runs beside him swinging a red mallet on a chain toward a red wall-mounted emergency box with a glass front. Inside the box, a blond man in a blue suit with a long red tie (caricature of Donald Trump) stands with arms crossed; the box is stenciled with the emergency-break-glass legend, and a speech bubble above Uncle Sam reads HURRY UP. Signed Tina Toon with a copyright credit along the bottom edge.

TYPE: meme
SUBJECT: A blue-bordered composite meme titled 10 DAYS OF DARKNESS built from stacked panels: top panel pairs a portrait of a bearded pope in red vestments seated in a chair with a short history-article snippet about the 1582 calendar switch; middle panel shows a Renaissance painting of an assembled council of robed clerics under a canopy with a social-media watermark; bottom panel is a black-on-white October 1582 calendar grid whose fourth and fifteenth dates are circled in red, with a red arrow drawn from the painting panel down to the circled dates implying the skipped days.
TEXT: 10 DAYS OF DARKNESS
On This Day: In 1582, October 5 Never Happened
October 05, 2011 06:00 AM by |indulgences| Staff
On Oct. 5, 1582, much of Europe replaced the Julian calendar with the Gregorian calendar; the switch required the 10 days after Oct. 4 to be skipped.
Pope Gregory XIII
Creation of the Gregorian Calendar
@TheRealKimShady
